questions.prompt: The House of Wisdom, a celebrated centre of translation and scholarship, stood in which city?
questions.fact: Greek works that survive today often do so because they were translated into Arabic there and only much later rendered back into Latin.

questions.prompt: Which type of rock forms from cooled molten material?
questions.fact: Cooling speed determines crystal size, so slow-cooling granite is coarse while fast-cooling basalt is fine-grained.

questions.prompt: Which long jumper's 1968 Olympic mark stood as the world record for 23 years?
questions.fact: The jump exceeded the optical measuring device's range, so officials had to find a tape measure while the crowd waited.

questions.prompt: Which streaming series follows office workers whose memories are surgically divided?
questions.fact: Its stark office set was built practically, and the show leans on symmetrical framing to make the corridors feel endless.

questions.prompt: Which country is crossed by both the equator and the Tropic of Capricorn?
questions.fact: It is the only country in the world crossed by both lines.

questions.prompt: Which form of Japanese poetry traditionally uses a five-seven-five pattern?
questions.fact: Classical examples usually include a seasonal reference and a cutting word that pivots the image.

questions.prompt: Which term describes software whose source code anyone may inspect and modify?
questions.fact: It is distinct from merely free of charge; the licence, not the price, is what defines it.
